MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

DATED: 14 October 2026

PARTIES:

(1) VANTIS ANALYTICS LIMITED, a company incorporated in England and Wales under company number 11849201, whose registered office is at 5th Floor, The Zig Zag Building, 70 Victoria Street, London SW1E 6SQ (Vantis); and

(2) HALYARD SOFTWARE LTD, a company incorporated in England and Wales under company number 09876543, whose registered office is at 12 Mill Lane, Manchester M1 2AB (Halyard).

Vantis and Halyard are each referred to as a Party and collectively as the Parties.

BACKGROUND:

The Parties intend to enter into discussions regarding a potential commercial arrangement or corporate transaction between them (the Purpose). In connection with the Purpose, each Party may disclose to the other confidential and proprietary technical, commercial, financial or operational information. The Parties agree to protect such information on the terms of this Agreement.

OPERATIVE PROVISIONS:

Definitions

1.1 In this Agreement, unless the context otherwise requires:

1.1.1 Agreement means this mutual non-disclosure agreement.

1.1.2 Business Day means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in England when clearing banks in the City of London are open for business.

1.1.3 Confidential Information means any and all information of a confidential, sensitive or proprietary nature (whether commercial, technical, operational, financial, administrative or otherwise) relating to a Party, which is disclosed or made available by or on behalf of that Party (the Disclosing Party) to the other Party (the Recipient), directly or indirectly, in written, electronic, oral, visual or any other tangible or intangible form, whether before, on or after the date of this Agreement, including all software code, product architecture, data models, algorithm designs, customer lists, pipeline figures, trade secrets, pricing models, and all derivative materials prepared by the Recipient containing or reflecting such information.

1.1.4 Disclosing Party has the meaning given in Clause 1.1.3.

1.1.5 Recipient has the meaning given in Clause 1.1.3.

Confidentiality Undertakings

2.1 In consideration of the mutual disclosure of Confidential Information, the Recipient agrees and undertakes that it shall:

2.1.1 treat all Confidential Information disclosed by the Disclosing Party as strictly confidential and preserve its confidentiality with at least the same degree of care as it uses for its own confidential information of a similar nature, but in no event less than a reasonable standard of care;

2.1.2 use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information solely and exclusively for the Purpose, and for no other commercial, developmental, testing or competitive purpose whatsoever;

2.1.3 keep the Confidential Information in safe and secure custody, preventing any unauthorised access, copying, disclosure or distribution; and

2.1.4 not copy, reproduce, reduce to writing or record the Confidential Information except to the extent strictly necessary for the Purpose.

Exclusions from Confidentiality

3.1 The obligations in Clause 2 shall not apply to any specific portion of Confidential Information that the Recipient can demonstrate to the reasonable satisfaction of the Disclosing Party:

3.1.1 is at the time of disclosure, or subsequently becomes, part of the public domain, provided that such availability in the public domain does not arise directly or indirectly from a breach of this Agreement or any other confidentiality obligation owed by any person; or

3.1.2 is received on an unrestricted basis after disclosure hereunder from an independent third party who, to the best of the Recipient's knowledge after diligent enquiry, is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of such information.

Permitted Access and Disclosure

4.1 The Recipient shall restrict access to the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information exclusively to those of its own direct employees who have a strict need to know such information for the performance of the Purpose. The Recipient shall not disclose, transmit or make available any Confidential Information to any other person, entity or organisation whatsoever, including any external legal, financial or tax advisers, auditors, insurers, sub-contractors or corporate affiliates of the Recipient.

4.2 The Recipient shall ensure that each of its employees having access to the Confidential Information is informed of its confidential nature and is bound by professional or contractual duties of confidentiality sufficient to enforce the obligations in this Agreement. The Recipient remains directly liable for any breach of this Agreement caused by the act or omission of any such employee.

4.3 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to the minimum extent required by an order of a court of competent jurisdiction or by mandatory statutory requirement, provided that the Recipient gives the Disclosing Party immediate written notice of such requirement (where legally permissible) to enable the Disclosing Party to seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy.

Knowledge and Residuals

5.1 Nothing in this Agreement shall restrict or prevent the Recipient from using or developing any ideas, concepts, know-how, methods or techniques retained in the unaided memory of its personnel who have had authorised access to the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information under this Agreement, and the Recipient shall have no liability in respect of any subsequent use or exploitation thereof, provided that such personnel do not intentionally memorize such information for the purpose of reproducing it.

Return and Destruction of Materials

6.1 Upon the written demand of the Disclosing Party at any time, or automatically upon the termination of discussions relating to the Purpose, the Recipient shall within five (5) Business Days:

6.1.1 return to the Disclosing Party, or securely destroy or erase, all documents, records, files, magnetic media and other tangible or electronic embodiments of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in its possession, custody or control; and

6.1.2 confirm in writing, signed by an authorised officer of the Recipient, that all such Confidential Information has been returned, deleted or destroyed in accordance with this Clause 6.1.

6.2 Notwithstanding Clause 6.1, the Recipient may retain one archival copy of the Confidential Information solely in off-site automated disaster recovery backups, provided that such retained copies shall remain subject to the obligations of this Agreement until destroyed in the ordinary course of the Recipient's automated retention cycle.

Proprietary Rights

7.1 All Confidential Information, including all intellectual property rights subsisting therein, shall remain the sole and exclusive property of the Disclosing Party or its third-party licensors.

7.2 No licence, assignment or transfer of any intellectual property right, proprietary right or right of use is granted or implied under this Agreement, save for the express limited right to review the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose.

7.3 All Confidential Information is furnished without warranty of any kind, whether express, implied or statutory, including warranties as to accuracy, completeness, non-infringement or fitness for purpose.

Term and Duration

8.1 This Agreement shall take effect from the date first written above and shall continue in force for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party upon giving fourteen (14) days' written notice to the other Party.

8.2 The obligations of confidentiality, non-use and non-disclosure set out in this Agreement shall survive the termination or expiry of this Agreement and shall remain binding on the Recipient for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of termination or expiry.

General Provisions

9.1 Injunctive Relief. The Parties acknowledge that money damages may be an inadequate remedy for any breach of this Agreement and that each Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief, specific performance or other equitable remedies in respect of any actual or threatened breach.

9.2 Entire Agreement. Heretofore and hereinafter, this Agreement, together with any schedules hereto, constitutes the entire and whole understanding and covenant between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, and notwithstanding the foregoing or any prior negotiations, supersedes, cancels, extinguishes and nullifies in its entirety all previous parol, oral, written or tacit representations, promises, assurances, warranties and agreements between the said Parties touching upon the premises.

9.3 Non-Assignment. Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer or subcontract any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party.

9.4 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal or unenforceable, the validity, legality and enforceability of the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired.

9.5 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which taken together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart via electronic signature or digital transmission shall be deemed legally binding.

9.6 Governing Law and Jurisdiction. This Agreement and any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with it or its subject matter or formation (including non-contractual disputes or claims) shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of England and Wales. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales to resolve any dispute or claim arising under or in connection with this Agreement.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF the Parties have executed this Agreement on the date first written above.
